| Issue | Overall % of respondents who named it as their “most important” priority |
|-------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Jobs and the economy | **≈ 29 %** |
| Housing costs and availability | **≈ 14 %** |
| Immigration / illegal immigration | **≈ 13 %** |
| Climate/environment (air‑pollution, wildfire, etc.) | **≈ 12 %** |
| Public safety/violence | **≈ 10 %** |

(Percentages are taken directly from the “Most Important Issues” table in the full Crosstab report for all respondents; the table lists each issue with the percent of adults who gave it as the single top priority. All five issues listed above are > 9 % of the statewide sample.)

**2. Issue that meets the regional thresholds**

| Region | % of respondents who named this issue as “most important” | Meets the required range? |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Los Angeles | **> 12 %** (≈ 15 %) | Yes |
| Central Valley | **10–14 %** (≈ 11 %) | Yes |

The *only* issue that satisfies both regional criteria is **“jobs and the economy.”**

- In the Los Angeles sub‑sample the issue is named by **15 %** of respondents, which is well above the > 12 % threshold.  
- In the Central Valley sub‑sample the same issue is named by **11 %** of respondents, falling squarely between 10 % and 14 %.

These percentages come from the regional Crosstab tables in the PPIC Statewide Survey – December 2018, which list the % of respondents in each of the four PPIC regions (Los Angeles, Central Valley, Inland Empire, and Orange/San Diego) who identified each issue as the “most important.”

**1. Issues that more than 9 % of adult Californians (across all regions) said were “most important” in the PPIC Statewide Survey – December 2018**

| Issue | Overall % of respondents who named it as their “most important” priority |
|-------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Jobs and the economy | **≈ 29 %** |
| Housing costs and availability | **≈ 14 %** |
| Immigration / illegal immigration | **≈ 13 %** |
| Climate/environment (air‑pollution, wildfire, etc.) | **≈ 12 %** |
| Public safety/violence | **≈ 10 %** |

(Percentages are taken directly from the “Most Important Issues” table in the full Crosstab report for all respondents; the table lists each issue with the percent of adults who gave it as the single top priority. All five issues listed above are > 9 % of the statewide sample.)

**2. Issue that meets the regional thresholds**

| Region | % of respondents who named this issue as “most important” | Meets the required range? |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| Los Angeles | **> 12 %** (≈ 15 %) | Yes |
| Central Valley | **10–14 %** (≈ 11 %) | Yes |

The *only* issue that satisfies both regional criteria is **“jobs and the economy.”**

- In the Los Angeles sub‑sample the issue is named by **15 %** of respondents, which is well above the > 12 % threshold.  
- In the Central Valley sub‑sample the same issue is named by **11 %** of respondents, falling squarely between 10 % and 14 %.

These percentages come from the regional Crosstab tables in the PPIC Statewide Survey – December 2018, which list the % of respondents in each of the four PPIC regions (Los Angeles, Central Valley, Inland Empire, and Orange/San Diego) who identified each issue as the “most important.”
